## Question 1

```{r}
# get countries with more than 200 records
ss_country_counts <- ss_df %>% count(Country) %>% filter(n > 200)

# select only these countries in a df
ss_countries_200 <- ss_df %>% filter(Country %in% ss_country_counts$Country)

# compute average shipping cost per country
ss_avg_ship_cost <- ss_countries_200 %>% group_by(Country) %>% 
  mutate(avg_ship_cost = mean(Shipping.Cost, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()

# filter the records with above average shipping cost 
ss_above_avg_ship <- ss_avg_ship_cost %>% filter(Shipping.Cost > avg_ship_cost)

# create new ratio
ss_ratio <- ss_above_avg_ship %>% mutate(ratio = Profit / Shipping.Cost)

# rank the top 15 records
q1_answers <- ss_ratio %>% arrange(desc(ratio)) %>%
  select(Customer.Name, Product.Name, Country, Sales, Profit, Shipping.Cost, ratio) %>%
  head(15)

q1_answers
```

## Question 2

```{r}
# remove transactions with zero or negative sales
ss_pos_sales <- ss_df %>% filter(Sales > 0)

# compute average profit and average sales per market-year
ss_avg_profit <- ss_pos_sales %>% 
  group_by(Market, Year) %>% 
  summarise(
    avg_profit = mean(Profit, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_sales = mean(Sales, na.rm = TRUE),
    order_count = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# keep market-year groups that have at least 50 orders
ss_groups_50 <- ss_avg_profit %>% 
  filter(order_count >= 50)

# compute overall median profit from the full dataset
ss_median_profit <- median(ss_df$Profit, na.rm = TRUE)

# get the markets where the yearly average profit never drops below median
ss_above_med_markets <- ss_groups_50 %>% 
  group_by(Market) %>% 
  filter(all(avg_profit >= ss_median_profit)) %>% 
  ungroup()

# compute average sales per market from the remaining group-level records
ss_market_avg_sales <- ss_above_med_markets %>%
  group_by(Market) %>%
  summarise(avg_sales_overall = mean(avg_sales), .groups = "drop")

# rank by descending average sales and show top 10
q2_answers <- ss_market_avg_sales %>% 
  arrange(desc(avg_sales_overall)) %>% 
  head(10)

q2_answers
```

## Question 3

```{r}
# compute IQR-based threshold for "unusually high" discount per sub-category
ss_discount_stats <- ss_df %>%
  group_by(Sub.Category) %>%
  summarise(
    q3_discount = quantile(Discount, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    iqr_discount = IQR(Discount, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# define unusually high as above Q3 + 1.5 * IQR (statistical outlier)
ss_discount_stats <- ss_discount_stats %>%
  mutate(high_threshold = q3_discount + 1.5 * iqr_discount)

# join threshold back to original df
ss_with_threshold <- ss_df %>%
  left_join(ss_discount_stats, by = "Sub.Category")

# flag records where discount is unusually high (above outlier threshold)
ss_sus <- ss_with_threshold %>%
  filter(Discount > high_threshold)

# label each suspicious record as loss-making or non-loss-making
ss_sus_labels <- ss_sus %>%
  mutate(label = ifelse(Profit < 0, "loss-making", "non-loss-making"))

# count suspicious records by market, segment and label
ss_counts <- ss_sus_labels %>%
  group_by(Market, Segment, label) %>%
  summarise(count = n(), .groups = "drop")

# compute total suspicious records per market-segment
ss_total_sus <- ss_sus_labels %>%
  group_by(Market, Segment) %>%
  summarise(total = n(), .groups = "drop")

# join counts with totals
ss_share <- ss_counts %>%
  left_join(ss_total_sus, by = c("Market", "Segment"))

# compute loss-making share
ss_share_pct <- ss_share %>%
  mutate(loss_share = count / total)

# keep only loss-making rows
ss_loss <- ss_share_pct %>%
  filter(label == "loss-making")

# keep only combinations where loss-making share is above 40%
ss_above_40 <- ss_loss %>%
  filter(loss_share > 0.40)

# sort from highest to lowest loss-making share
q3_answers <- ss_above_40 %>%
  arrange(desc(loss_share))

q3_answers
```

## Question 4

```{r}
# initialise variables to stop at
running_total <- 0
stop_at_row <- NA
stop_at_order_id <- NA
stop_at_customer <- NA

# loop through each row in dataset order
for (i in 1:nrow(ss_df)) {
  
  # skip rows where quantity is less than 2
  if (ss_df$Quantity[i] < 2) next
  running_total <- running_total + ss_df$Profit[i] # sum up 
  
  # check if total exceeds 25000
  if (running_total > 25000) {
    stop_at_row <- i
    stop_at_order_id <- ss_df$Order.ID[i]
    stop_at_customer <- ss_df$Customer.Name[i]
    break
  }
}

# results for dataset order
cat("----- Original dataset order -----\n")
cat("Stop at row:", stop_at_row, "\n")
cat("Order ID:", stop_at_order_id, "\n")
cat("Customer name:", stop_at_customer, "\n")
cat("Running total:", running_total, "\n")
cat("\n")

# reorder dataset by sales descending
ss_desc_df <- ss_df %>% arrange(desc(Sales))

# reinitialise variables to stop at
running_total_desc <- 0
stop_at_row_desc <- NA
stop_at_order_id_desc <- NA
stop_at_customer_desc <- NA

# loop through each row in descending order
for (i in 1:nrow(ss_desc_df)) {
  
  # skip rows where quantity is less than 2
  if (ss_desc_df$Quantity[i] < 2) next
  
  # sum up running total
  running_total_desc <- running_total_desc + ss_desc_df$Profit[i]
  
  # check if total exceeds 25000
  if (running_total_desc > 25000) {
    stop_at_row_desc <- i
    stop_at_order_id_desc <- ss_desc_df$Order.ID[i]
    stop_at_customer_desc <- ss_desc_df$Customer.Name[i]
    break
  }
}

# results for descending sales order
cat("----- Sorted by descending sales order -----\n")
cat("Stop at row:", stop_at_row_desc, "\n")
cat("Order ID:", stop_at_order_id_desc, "\n")
cat("Customer name:", stop_at_customer_desc, "\n")
cat("Running total:", running_total_desc, "\n")
```

## Question 5

```{r}
# count distinct countries per product
ss_country_count <- ss_df %>%
  group_by(Product.Name) %>%
  summarise(country_count = n_distinct(Country))

# keep only products sold in at least 4 different countries
ss_products_4 <- ss_country_count %>%
  filter(country_count >= 4)

# get the product names
ss_product_names <- ss_products_4$Product.Name

# filter main df to only those products
ss_resilient_df <- ss_df %>%
  filter(Product.Name %in% ss_product_names)

# compute median discount per product
ss_product_median_discount <- ss_resilient_df %>%
  group_by(Product.Name) %>%
  summarise(median_discount = median(Discount, na.rm = TRUE))

# join median discount back to filtered df
ss_resilient_with_median <- ss_resilient_df %>%
  left_join(ss_product_median_discount, by = "Product.Name")

# split into high discount records
ss_high_discount <- ss_resilient_with_median %>%
  filter(Discount > median_discount)

# split into low discount records
ss_low_discount <- ss_resilient_with_median %>%
  filter(Discount <= median_discount)

# compute average profit for high discount records per product
ss_avg_profit_high <- ss_high_discount %>%
  group_by(Product.Name) %>%
  summarise(avg_profit_high = mean(Profit, na.rm = TRUE))

# compute average profit for low discount records per product
ss_avg_profit_low <- ss_low_discount %>%
  group_by(Product.Name) %>%
  summarise(avg_profit_low = mean(Profit, na.rm = TRUE))

# join high and low average profits together
ss_profit_compare <- ss_avg_profit_high %>%
  inner_join(ss_avg_profit_low, by = "Product.Name")

# compute the gap between high and low discount average profit
ss_profit_gap <- ss_profit_compare %>%
  mutate(gap = avg_profit_high - avg_profit_low)

# keep only products where high discount condition performs better
ss_resilient_products <- ss_profit_gap %>%
  filter(gap > 0)

# order by size of gap and show top 5
q5_answers <- ss_resilient_products %>%
  arrange(desc(gap)) %>%
  head(5)

q5_answers
```

## Question 6

```{r}
# compute total sales per market
ss_market_sales <- ss_df %>%
  group_by(Market) %>%
  summarise(market_total_sales = sum(Sales, na.rm = TRUE))

# compute total sales per market and city
ss_city_sales <- ss_df %>%
  group_by(Market, City) %>%
  summarise(city_total_sales = sum(Sales, na.rm = TRUE))

# join city sales with market total sales
ss_city_share <- ss_city_sales %>%
  left_join(ss_market_sales, by = "Market")

# compute each city's share of its market's sales
ss_city_share_pct <- ss_city_share %>%
  mutate(city_share = city_total_sales / market_total_sales)

# join city share back to original df to get segment info
ss_with_share <- ss_df %>%
  left_join(ss_city_share_pct, by = c("Market", "City"))

# get distinct market, city, segment, city_share combinations
ss_city_segment_share <- ss_with_share %>%
  select(Market, City, Segment, city_share) %>%
  distinct()

# for each market and segment, find the city with the greatest share
ss_dominant_city <- ss_city_segment_share %>%
  group_by(Market, Segment) %>%
  filter(city_share == max(city_share))

# keep only cases where one city contributes more than one third of market sales
ss_above_third <- ss_dominant_city %>%
  filter(city_share > 1/3)

# sort by descending sales share and show top 10
q6_answers <- ss_above_third %>%
  arrange(desc(city_share)) %>%
  select(Market, Segment, City, city_share) %>%
  head(10)

q6_answers

# Explanation: No city is found to contribute more than one-third (33.3%) of its
# market's total sales. The highest city-level share is approximately 12.4%, 
# which is Montréal within the Canada market.
```

## Question 7

```{r}
# extract month from order date and filter for Q4 (Oct, Nov, Dec)
ss_q4 <- ss_df %>%
  mutate(month = as.integer(format(Order.Date, "%m"))) %>%
  filter(month %in% c(10, 11, 12))

# create profitability score that penalizes discount and shipping cost
ss_scored <- ss_q4 %>%
  mutate(profit_score = Profit - (Discount * Sales) - Shipping.Cost)

# compute total score per product within each region and year
ss_product_scores <- ss_scored %>%
  group_by(Region, Year, Product.Name) %>%
  summarise(total_score = sum(profit_score, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# find top scoring product per region and year (allow ties)
ss_top_products <- ss_product_scores %>%
  group_by(Region, Year) %>%
  slice_max(total_score, with_ties = TRUE) %>%
  ungroup()

# count how many times each product appears as top scorer within each region
ss_product_count <- ss_top_products %>%
  group_by(Region, Product.Name) %>%
  summarise(times_top = n(), .groups = "drop")

# keep all products with max frequency per region (allow ties)
ss_most_frequent <- ss_product_count %>%
  group_by(Region) %>%
  filter(times_top == max(times_top)) %>%
  ungroup()

# arrange by region
q7_answers <- ss_most_frequent %>%
  arrange(Region, desc(times_top))

View(q7_answers)
```

## Question 8

```{r}
# compute shipping days
ss_ship <- ss_df %>%
  mutate(ship_days = as.numeric(as.Date(Ship.Date) - as.Date(Order.Date)))

# remove records with missing or impossible date gaps
ss_ship_clean <- ss_ship %>%
  filter(!is.na(ship_days) & ship_days >= 0)

# convert priority into numeric levels (higher number = higher urgency)
ss_ship_clean <- ss_ship_clean %>%
  mutate(priority_level = case_when(
    Order.Priority == "Low" ~ 1,
    Order.Priority == "Medium" ~ 2,
    Order.Priority == "High" ~ 3,
    Order.Priority == "Critical" ~ 4
  ))

# compute average ship days per ship mode and priority level
ss_avg_ship_days <- ss_ship_clean %>%
  group_by(Ship.Mode, priority_level) %>%
  summarise(avg_days = mean(ship_days, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# compare all priority pairs within the same ship mode
ss_comparison <- ss_avg_ship_days %>%
  inner_join(ss_avg_ship_days, by = "Ship.Mode", suffix = c("_low", "_high"), relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  filter(priority_level_low < priority_level_high & avg_days_low < avg_days_high)

# get all distinct ship modes
ss_all_modes <- ss_ship_clean %>%
  distinct(Ship.Mode)

# count surprising cases per ship mode (including 0 cases)
q8_answers <- ss_comparison %>%
  group_by(Ship.Mode) %>%
  summarise(surprise_count = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  right_join(ss_all_modes, by = "Ship.Mode") %>%
  mutate(surprise_count = ifelse(is.na(surprise_count), 0, surprise_count)) %>%
  arrange(desc(surprise_count))

q8_answers
```

## Question 9

```{r}
# compute total sales and profit per year and week
ss_weekly <- ss_df %>%
  group_by(Year, weeknum) %>%
  summarise(
    week_sales = sum(Sales, na.rm = TRUE),
    week_profit = sum(Profit, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# compute total valid sales per year (only non-negative profit weeks)
ss_year_total <- ss_weekly %>%
  filter(week_profit >= 0) %>%
  group_by(Year) %>%
  summarise(year_total_sales = sum(week_sales, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# get unique years sorted
ss_years <- sort(unique(ss_df$Year))

# initialise empty vectors to store results
result_years <- c()
result_trigger_week <- c()
result_cum_sales <- c()
result_weeks_counted <- c()

# loop through each year
for (yr in ss_years) {
  
  # get ALL weeks for this year sorted by week number
  ss_yr_weeks <- ss_weekly %>%
    filter(Year == yr) %>%
    arrange(weeknum)
  
  # get 20% threshold for this year
  ss_yr_threshold <- ss_year_total %>%
    filter(Year == yr) %>%
    pull(year_total_sales) * 0.20
  
  # initialise tracking variables
  cum_sales <- 0
  weeks_counted <- 0
  trigger_week <- NA
  
  # loop through each week in order
  for (i in 1:nrow(ss_yr_weeks)) {
    
    # skip weeks where profit is negative
    if (ss_yr_weeks$week_profit[i] < 0) next
    
    # add week sales to cumulative total
    cum_sales <- cum_sales + ss_yr_weeks$week_sales[i]
    
    # increment weeks counted
    weeks_counted <- weeks_counted + 1
    
    # check if cumulative sales exceed 20% threshold
    if (cum_sales > ss_yr_threshold) {
      trigger_week <- ss_yr_weeks$weeknum[i]
      break
    }
  }
  
  # append results to vectors
  result_years <- c(result_years, yr)
  result_trigger_week <- c(result_trigger_week, trigger_week)
  result_cum_sales <- c(result_cum_sales, cum_sales)
  result_weeks_counted <- c(result_weeks_counted, weeks_counted)
}

# combine vectors into a dataframe
ss_results <- data.frame(
  Year = result_years,
  trigger_week = result_trigger_week,
  cumulative_sales = result_cum_sales,
  weeks_counted = result_weeks_counted
)

# sort by year
q9_answers <- ss_results %>%
  arrange(Year)

q9_answers
```

## Question 10

```{r}
# aggregate totals at region, state and sub-category level
ss_state_subcat <- ss_df %>%
  group_by(Region, State, Sub.Category) %>%
  summarise(
    row_count = n(),
    total_profit = sum(Profit, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_sales = sum(Sales, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_shipping = sum(Shipping.Cost, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_quantity = sum(Quantity, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# keep only combinations with at least 30 rows
ss_state_subcat_30 <- ss_state_subcat %>%
  filter(row_count >= 30)

# create profitability and shipping per unit metrics from totals
ss_with_metrics <- ss_state_subcat_30 %>%
  mutate(
    profit_ratio = total_profit / total_sales,
    ship_per_unit = total_shipping / total_quantity
  )

# compute dataset wide average profit ratio from group-level data
ss_avg_profit_ratio <- mean(ss_with_metrics$profit_ratio, na.rm = TRUE)

# compute dataset wide average shipping cost per unit from group-level data
ss_avg_ship_per_unit <- mean(ss_with_metrics$ship_per_unit, na.rm = TRUE)

# keep combinations below average profit ratio and above average shipping per unit
ss_underperformers <- ss_with_metrics %>%
  filter(
    profit_ratio < ss_avg_profit_ratio &
    ship_per_unit > ss_avg_ship_per_unit
  )

# rank by worst profitability within each region and keep top 3
ss_top3 <- ss_underperformers %>%
  group_by(Region) %>%
  arrange(profit_ratio) %>%
  slice_head(n = 3) %>%
  ungroup()

# select relevant columns and sort by region
q10_answers <- ss_top3 %>%
  select(Region, State, Sub.Category, profit_ratio, ship_per_unit) %>%
  arrange(Region)

q10_answers
```
